builtin.fc.env-histfile-initialization.reason: Entirely implementation-defined: "An implementation may choose to access the HISTFILE variable only when initializing the history file", and "it is implementation-defined whether changes made to HISTFILE after the history file has been initialized are effective". Whether a mid-session assignment to HISTFILE takes effect therefore cannot be asserted either way; that HISTFILE names the history file at all is asserted by blt2-fc-histfile-names-history-file.

builtin.fc.env-histfile-sharing-and-dele.reason: Explicitly unspecified at both ends: "it is unspecified how updates to the history file from those shells interact" and "It is unspecified when history file entries are physically removed from the history file". The residual ordering requirement (oldest deleted first) becomes observable only once the history file has reached its implementation-defined size, which no portable command sequence can force.
